title.en: Find the emf of a rod rotating in a magnetic field.

say.en: Slide a metal rod across a magnetic field and a voltage appears between its ends, with no battery anywhere. The magnetic force pushes the free electrons along the rod. In this lesson: Derive and use epsilon equals Blv.
Find the emf of a rod rotating in a magnetic field.

body.en: A rod of length l *moving* with velocity v perpendicular to a uniform field B (with l, v and B mutually perpendicular) develops $\varepsilon = Blv$. It can be seen as the rate of change of flux through the circuit, or as the Lorentz force qvB pushing charges along the rod. If the rod slides on rails closing a circuit of resistance R, the current is Blv/R and the field exerts a retarding force $B^2l^2v/R$; an external force must supply power $B^2l^2v^2/R$, which becomes heat.
body.kn: B ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ v ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುವ l ಉದ್ದದ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ε = Blv. R ರೋಧದ ಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ Blv/R; ಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುವ ಬಲ B²l²v/R.

points.en: ε = Blv (l, v, B mutually perpendicular)

narration.en: A rod of length l moving at speed v across a field B develops an emf B l v. In a circuit of resistance R this drives a current B l v by R, and a force B squared l squared v by R opposes the motion.
narration.kn: B ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ v ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುವ l ಉದ್ದದ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ε = Blv. R ರೋಧದ ಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ Blv/R; ಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುವ ಬಲ B²l²v/R.

say.en: A rod of length l moving at speed v across a field B develops an emf B l v. In a circuit of resistance R this drives a current B l v by R, and a force B squared l squared v by R opposes the motion. epsilon equals Blv (l, v, B mutually perpendicular).
say.kn: B ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ v ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಲಿಸುವ l ಉದ್ದದ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ epsilon equals Blv. R ರೋಧದ ಮಂಡಲದಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರವಾಹ Blv/R; ಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುವ ಬಲ B squaredl squaredv/R.

say.en: I equals Blv/R.
Retarding force F equals B squaredl squaredv/R.

narration.en: A rod of length l slides at speed v along two rails, in a field B into the page. The flux through the circuit is Φ = Blx; as x grows at rate v, the emf is ε = Blv. A current I = Blv/R flows, and the field pushes back on the rod with F = B²l²v/R, so you must keep pulling. Your pulling power Fv equals the heating ε²/R in the resistor: energy is conserved. A rod of length l spinning at ω about one end sweeps out area, giving ε = ½Bωl². Example: a 1 m rod turning 50 times a second in 1 T gives ε = ½ × 1 × 100π × 1 ≈ 157 V.

A rod of length l slides at speed v along two rails, in a field B into the page. The flux through the circuit is Φ equals Blx; as x grows at rate v, the emf is epsilon equals Blv. A current I equals Blv/R flows, and the field pushes back on the rod with F equals B squaredl squaredv/R, so you must keep pulling. Your pulling power Fv equals the heating epsilon squared/R in the resistor: energy is conserved. A rod of length l spinning at omega about one end sweeps out area, giving epsilon equals one half B omega l squared. Example: a 1 metre rod turning 50 times a second in 1 T gives epsilon equals one half times 1 times 100 pi times 1 is approximately 157 volts.

title.en: A rod sliding on rails in a magnetic field
title.kn: ಕಾಂತ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಳಿಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಜಾರುವ ಸರಳು

narration.en: The moving rod cuts the field: emf ε = Blv drives a current I = ε/R round the circuit. The field then pushes on the current with F = BIl, opposing the motion. Keep pushing and the force you apply supplies the power εI. Let go and the rod slows down, as Lenz's law says. Rod mass 0.1 kg.
narration.kn: ಕಾಂತ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರದಲ್ಲಿ ಹಳಿಗಳ ಮೇಲೆ ಜಾರುವ ಸರಳು. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

caption.kn: ಚಲಿಸುವ ಸರಳು ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವನ್ನು ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: emf ε = Blv, ಪ್ರವಾಹ I = ε/R. ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರ ಪ್ರವಾಹದ ಮೇಲೆ F = BIl ಬಲ ಹಾಕಿ ಚಲನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿರೋಧಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ತಳ್ಳುತ್ತಿದ್ದರೆ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಬಲ εI ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಬಿಟ್ಟರೆ ಸರಳು ನಿಧಾನವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಸರಳಿನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ 0.1 kg.

Keep pushing and the force you apply supplies the power epsilon I. Let go and the rod slows down, as Lenz's law says. Rod mass 0.1 kilograms.

body.en: A rod of length l *rotating* with angular speed ω about one end, in a plane perpendicular to B, has speed ωx at distance x from the pivot. Adding up Bv dx along the rod gives $\varepsilon = \frac12B\omega l^2$, the same as Blv with the average speed ωl/2.
body.kn: ಒಂದು ತುದಿಯ ಸುತ್ತ ω ಕೋನೀಯ ವೇಗದಲ್ಲಿ ತಿರುಗುವ l ಉದ್ದದ ಸರಳಿನಲ್ಲಿ ε = ½Bωl².

points.en: Average speed of the rod = ωl/2

narration.en: A rod rotating about one end in a perpendicular field develops an emf of half B omega l squared, which is B l times its average speed.

Changing flux through a bulk conductor induces swirling currents inside it. They heat the metal and oppose motion.

problem.en: A rod 0.5 m long slides at 4 m s⁻¹ on rails across a field of 0.2 T. The circuit resistance is 2 Ω. Find the emf, the current and the force needed to keep the rod moving steadily.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A rod 0.5 m long slides at 4 m s⁻¹ on rails across a field of 0.2 T. The circuit resistance is 2 Ω. Find the emf, the current and the force needed to keep the rod moving steadily.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A rod 0.5 metres long slides at 4 metres s to the power minus 1 on rails across a field of 0.2 T. The circuit resistance is 2 ohms. Find the emf, the current and the force needed to keep the rod moving steadily.
epsilon equals Blv equals 0.2 times 0.5 times 4 equals 0.4 volts.
I equals epsilon /R equals 0.4 over 2 equals 0.2 A.
F equals BIl equals 0.2 times 0.2 times 0.5 equals 0.02 newtons.
So the answer is 0.4 volts; 0.2 A; 0.02 newtons.

problem.en: A metal rod 1 m long rotates at 400 rad s⁻¹ about one end in a plane perpendicular to a field of 0.5 T. Find the emf between its ends.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A metal rod 1 m long rotates at 400 rad s⁻¹ about one end in a plane perpendicular to a field of 0.5 T. Find the emf between its ends.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A metal rod 1 metre long rotates at 400 rad s to the power minus 1 about one end in a plane perpendicular to a field of 0.5 T. Find the emf between its ends.
epsilon equals one half B omega l squared.
epsilon equals one half times 0.5 times 400 times 1 squared.
epsilon equals 100 volts.
So the answer is 100 volts.

body.en: ε = Blv needs the rod, its velocity and the field all at right angles. If the rod moves along its own length, or along B, or lies along B, the emf is zero.
